body.statement:
Consider the one-cohort, two-return specialization \(S=1\) and \(H=1\), so that \(d=2p\), and fix
\[
 z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\cap[\delta_0,1-\delta_0]^d.
\]
Suppose, in addition to \(0<a_{\mathrm w}<1\), that
\[
 B\ge d^2,\qquad
 \inf_{\rho\in\mathcal R}\inf_{x\in[0,1]^d}
 \left[2a_{\mathrm w}^2\{1+\rho(x)\}
       +a_{\mathrm w}^4\{1-\rho(x)^2\}\right]\ge B^{-1},
 \qquad
 \{1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L).
\]
Then the construction in \texttt{def:mean-only-witness} has a common completion for which the \(\rho\)-indexed, relatively open family
\[
 \{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(\lambda).
\]
For every \(\rho\in\mathcal R\) and \(x\in[0,1]^d\), the untreated return-coordinate means are zero and their conditional coordinate marginals do not depend on \(\rho\), whereas
\[
 m_1^{P_\rho}(x)
 =\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]
 =1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(x),
 \qquad
 \tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)=-a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(z_0).
\]
There consequently exist \(\rho^{(0)},\rho^{(1)}\in\mathcal R\) such that \(\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\ne\rho^{(1)}(z_0)\),
\[
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(0)}})
 =\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(1)}}),
 \qquad
 \left|\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(1)}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(0)}}}(z_0)\right|
 =a_{\mathrm w}^2\left|\rho^{(1)}(z_0)-\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\right|>0.
\]
Thus \(\tau_n\) is not a functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\) on this submodel. This conclusion concerns only mean-only return-path matching; it does not assert observational equivalence under the full historical wealth panel.
body.justification: The result isolates the information loss from discarding within-path dependence without denying identification from the maintained full wealth panel.
body.gap: Barber--Lyon and Goldsmith-Pinkham--Lyu diagnose volatility drag; this proposition gives an explicit two-law, relatively open nonidentification result for the restricted mean-only map while preserving full-panel identification under event transport.
body.consumer: Analysts can determine whether a return-matching procedure discards dependence information needed for a finite-cohort compounded-wealth effect.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(a=a_{\mathrm w}\).  We give a common measurable scaffolding, conditional on \(E_0\), on which only the sign-pair kernels vary with \(\rho\in\mathcal R\).  Fix the displayed
\[
z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\cap[\delta_0,1-\delta_0]^d.
\]
Let \(X_{1t}\), \(t=1,\ldots,T\), be independent uniform random vectors on \([0,1]^d\), conditional on \(E_0\).  Conditional on the complete design and \(E_0\), draw the historical sign pairs independently over \((t,i)\) according to
\[
P_\rho(U_{1ti}=u,V_{1ti}=v\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
=\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4},
\qquad (u,v)\in\{-1,1\}^2.
\]
The defining bound \(\sup_x|\rho(x)|\le 1-2\delta_0\) for \(\mathcal R\) implies
\[
\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4}\ge \frac{1-\lvert\rho(x)\rvert}{4}
\ge\frac{\delta_0}{2}>0,
\]
and summing the four displayed masses gives one.  Thus this is a well-defined, everywhere-positive conditional kernel.  Independently over \(i\), and independently of all historical variables given \(E_0\), draw \((U_{1i},V_{1i})\) from the same kernel evaluated at \(x=z_0\); use that kernel for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\) to specify the regular conditional event-sign law away from the realized point as well.  Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
B_{1i}(0)&=(1+aU_{1i})(1+aV_{1i}),
&B_{1i}(1)&=B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=1,\\
Q_{1ti}(0)&=Q_{1ti}(1)=Q_{1ti},
&Q_{1ti}&=(1+aU_{1ti})(1+aV_{1ti}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Set \(W_{1i,-1}=1\), \(R_{1i0}(0)=aU_{1i}\), \(R_{1i1}(0)=aV_{1i}\), and \(R_{1ih}(1)=0\) for \(h=0,1\).  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level}, these choices give the displayed values of \(B_{1i}(0)\) and \(B_{1i}(1)\).  Since \(0<a<1\), every return is strictly larger than \(-1\).  For every other-unit assignment vector, set
\[
B_{1i}(b,\mathbf a_{-1i})=B_{1i}(b),\qquad b\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The preceding equations verify \texttt{ass:consistency}, \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}, \texttt{ass:no-spillovers}, and \texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}.

We next complete the donor law without replacing the full covariance by coordinatewise variances.  Because \(S=1\), the stacked donor dimension is \(Sd=d\).  Conditional on \(E_0\), let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) be independent and uniform on the Euclidean sphere of radius \(\sqrt d\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), independent of the complete historical and event panels, and put
\[
Z_j=z_0+\xi_j.
\]
For any orthogonal matrix \(O\), rotational invariance gives \(O\xi_j\overset d=\xi_j\).  Hence \(\mathbb E(\xi_j\mid E_0)=0\), and \(A:=\mathbb E(\xi_j\xi_j^\top\mid E_0)\) commutes with every orthogonal matrix, so \(A=cI_d\) for some \(c\).  Taking traces yields
\[
dc=\operatorname{tr}(A)
=\mathbb E(\lVert\xi_j\rVert_2^2\mid E_0)=d,
\]
and therefore
\[
\mathbb E(Z_j\mid E_0)=z_0,
\qquad
\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid E_0)=I_d.
\]
In particular \(\Sigma\) has rank \(d\), and the declared ranges \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\) imply
\[
c_\Sigma I_d\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_d.
\]
Moreover, the hypothesis \(B\ge d^2\) gives
\[
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}\!\left[
 \left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\right\|_2^4
 \mathrel{\big|}E_0\right]
=\mathbb E(\lVert\xi_j\rVert_2^4\mid E_0)
=d^2\le B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:donor-replication}, \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, and \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} all hold for the full stacked donor path.

We now compute the historical response surface rather than identifying it by definition.  Summing the four-point kernel gives, for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(U_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)&=0,\\
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)&=0,\\
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(U_{1ti}V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)&=\rho(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
&=\mathbb E_{P_\rho}\!\left[
1+a(U_{1ti}+V_{1ti})+a^2U_{1ti}V_{1ti}
\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\right]\\
&=1+a^2\rho(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus, by \texttt{ass:historical-regression}, the regression surface is
\[
m_1^{P_\rho}(x)=1+a^2\rho(x).
\]
The compatibility hypothesis \(\{1+a^2\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}\subset\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) verifies \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}.  Since \(H=1\) and \(p\ge1\), the identity \(d=p(H+1)\) gives \(d=2p\ge2\).  Hence
\[
0<(1-a)^2\le Q_{1ti}\le(1+a)^2<4\le d^2\le B.
\]
The same inequalities hold for \(B_{1i}(0)\), while \(B_{1i}(1)=1\le B\).  This proves \texttt{ass:bounded-historical-wealth} and \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}.

The maintained class does not require a common within-site response law or a response-variance lower bound, but this particular witness has both properties.  Indeed, its conditional kernel is the same for every \(i\).  Also, for \(r=\rho(x)\), write \(U=U_{1ti}\) and \(V=V_{1ti}\).  The identities
\[
\mathbb E(U+V)=0,
\quad \mathbb E(UV)=r,
\quad (U+V)^2=2+2UV,
\quad (U+V)UV=U+V
\]
hold under the conditional kernel at \(x\).  Since subtracting the conditional mean does not change variance,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_{P_\rho}(Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
&=\operatorname{Var}\{a(U+V)+a^2UV\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}\\
&=a^2\mathbb E\{(U+V)^2\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}
  +a^4\operatorname{Var}(UV\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)\\
&\quad+2a^3\mathbb E\{(U+V)(UV-r)\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}\\
&=2a^2(1+r)+a^4(1-r^2).
\end{aligned}
\]
The cross term is zero because \(\mathbb E\{(U+V)UV\}=\mathbb E(U+V)=0\).  The displayed hypothesis in the proposition therefore implies that this variance is at least \(B^{-1}\), uniformly in \(\rho\) and \(x\).  This calculation merely certifies nondegeneracy of the selected lower-bound witness; it is not invoked as a restriction on the enlarged panel-law class.

It remains to verify the other class conditions.  The uniform design has density one, so the declared inequalities \(c_X\le1\le C_X\) imply \texttt{ass:design-density}.  Conditional independence of the complete unit-level sign collections over \(i\), together with the independent event collections, gives \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} after conditioning on the complete design and \(E_0\).  The design and historical sign pairs were drawn independently across \(t\), so the complete calendar vectors are conditionally independent across time; in particular, the historical design sequence \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^T\) is conditionally independent.  Therefore its absolute-regularity coefficients satisfy
\[
\beta_{P_\rho}(k\mid E_0)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
\qquad k\ge1,
\]
which is the design-only form of \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}; no restriction on within-unit temporal outcome dependence is used.  Set \(X_{1t}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{1t}\) to obtain \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}.  The stipulated location of \(z_0\) gives
\[
\operatorname{dist}(z_0,\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
\]
and hence \texttt{ass:interior-event-path}.  Choose the conditional event state to be degenerate at this admissible configuration.  Then
\[
P_\rho\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\ge c_X,
\]
so \texttt{ass:positive-query-region} holds.  Finally, the definition of \(\mathcal R\) states that the induced surface \(x\mapsto1+a^2\rho(x)\) satisfies the maintained two-sided covariance-standardized local-modulus inequalities.  Since the full covariance just calculated is \(I_d\), this is exactly \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}, with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

For event transport, the untreated event signs have the historical kernel evaluated at \(z_0\).  Applying the preceding conditional-mean calculation at that point gives, for every \(i\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=1+a^2\rho(z_0)
=m_1^{P_\rho}(z_0).
\]
Averaging over \(i=1,\ldots,n_1\) proves \texttt{ass:event-transport}.  We have verified every member property in \texttt{def:panel-law-class}.  The construction additionally has common within-site conditional laws and nondegenerate conditional response variance, although neither property restricts the enlarged class.  Hence
\[
\{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
\subset\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(\lambda).
\]
The indexing set is nonempty and relatively open by the definition of \(\mathcal R\).

We next derive the causal estimand and keep it distinct from the observed historical regression.  Since \(S=1\) and \(\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s=1\), one has \(\pi_1=1\).  By \texttt{def:target}, the potential-outcome construction, and the event-transport identity just proved,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)
&=\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]\\
&=1-\{1+a^2\rho(z_0)\}\\
&=-a^2\rho(z_0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the causal equality follows from potential outcomes and event transport; it is not introduced as an observed-law definition.

We finally compare the restricted information maps.  Marginalizing the sign-pair kernel yields
\[
P_\rho(U=u\mid x,E_0)
=\sum_{v\in\{-1,1\}}\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4}
=\frac12,
\qquad
P_\rho(V=v\mid x,E_0)=\frac12.
\]
Therefore each untreated return coordinate has, conditional on every \(x\), the common symmetric distribution on \(\{-a,a\}\), and in particular conditional mean zero.  Every treated return coordinate is identically zero.  The initial-wealth law is the common point mass at one, and
\[
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]=1
\]
for every \(\rho\).  It follows directly from \texttt{def:mean-only-information} that \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_\rho)\) is constant over \(\rho\in\mathcal R\).

It remains to show that this constant-information family contains a target-separated pair.  Choose \(\rho_*\in\mathcal R\), possible because \(\mathcal R\ne\varnothing\).  Relative openness in the Holder ball supplies \(\epsilon>0\) such that
\[
\left\{g\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L):
\lVert g-\rho_*\rVert_{\mathcal H_d}<\epsilon\right\}
\subset\mathcal R.
\]
There is a constant function \(c\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) with \(c\ne\rho_*(z_0)\): among two distinct constants of sufficiently small absolute value, at most one equals \(\rho_*(z_0)\).  For \(0<\eta<1\), define
\[
\rho_\eta=(1-\eta)\rho_*+\eta c.
\]
The Holder ball is convex, so \(\rho_\eta\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and
\[
\lVert\rho_\eta-\rho_*\rVert_{\mathcal H_d}
=\eta\lVert c-\rho_*\rVert_{\mathcal H_d}<\epsilon
\]
for every sufficiently small \(\eta>0\).  Hence \(\rho_\eta\in\mathcal R\), while
\[
\rho_\eta(z_0)-\rho_*(z_0)
=\eta\{c-\rho_*(z_0)\}\ne0.
\]
Set \(\rho^{(0)}=\rho_*\) and \(\rho^{(1)}=\rho_\eta\).  Constancy of the restricted information map gives
\[
\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(0)}})
=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(1)}}),
\]
whereas the causal-target formula gives
\[
\left|\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(1)}}}(z_0)
-\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(0)}}}(z_0)\right|
=a^2\left|\rho^{(1)}(z_0)-\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\right|>0.
\]
No functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\) can therefore equal \(\tau_n\) throughout this submodel.  The full historical wealth laws need not be equal: the joint sign kernel, and generally the conditional law of \(Q_{1ti}\), varies with \(\rho\).  The obstruction is exactly loss of within-path dependence information under the restricted mean-only map, as claimed.
